clue.text: US city mail misplaced singer’s gift? (10)

indicators.note: the letters are put in the wrong places, so rearrange them

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: An American city's post has gone astray, perhaps a present meant for a singer.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark sits on 'gift', which looks like a parcel in the post but means a talent.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: musicality, a feel for melody and pitch, is the natural talent a singer is gifted with.

clue.text: Big shock! Entertainers primarily manifest blue humour (4)

indicators.note: take the word's first letter

blocks.note: a mop is a big shock (thick mass) of hair
first letter of Entertainers

explanation.surface: A startling moment when performers put on a show of dark comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' reads as a fright, but here it is a shock of hair; 'blue humour' reads as smut, but it is a low mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase for a verb: 'blue' is low-spirited and 'humour' is mood, so to manifest blue humour is to sulk listlessly.

clue.text: Ogre eating European and Chinese character in Disney film (5,4)

indicators.note: the ogre takes E inside it

blocks.note: Shrek is the famous film ogre
E = European, placed inside SHREK after SH
the Han are China's majority people

explanation.surface: A cartoon ogre eating a European, with a Chinese figure, all in one animated film.
explanation.walkthrough: Shrek is a DreamWorks film, not Disney, so the ogre is a decoy: Shere Khan is the tiger in Disney's The Jungle Book.
explanation.definitionFit: Shere Khan is the tiger in Disney's animated The Jungle Book.

clue.text: Snazzy car’s collecting Republican that’s gone inside to moot (14)

indicators.note: a collector gathers things in, so the car takes the next piece into itself
the Republican has gone into the next word, so R sits within TO

blocks.note: a convertible is a flashy open-topped car
R = Republican
used as it is, with R inside: TRO, which goes in after CON

explanation.surface: A flashy car has picked up a Republican politician who has got in, heading off to a debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moot' is the adjective here, meaning open to argument, not the verb 'to raise for discussion'.
explanation.definitionFit: A moot point is one that can be argued either way, which is what controvertible means.

clue.text: Tips for mishandling archaeological disinterments? First, dig furiously (4,3)

indicators.note: the tips of the next three words are their first letters
the piece it goes with is put at the front

blocks.note: to dig something is slang for liking it
first letters of mishandling, archaeological, disinterments

explanation.surface: Advice on how to wreck an excavation: just start digging frantically.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as advice for archaeologists, but 'Tips' is an instruction to take first letters, and 'dig' is slang for like.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something like mad is to do it furiously, with frantic energy.

clue.text: Wreck extract of capsaicin at Italian’s counter (7)

indicators.note: the answer is drawn out of the words that follow
run the letters counter to the reading direction, that is backwards

blocks.note: the letters sit inside capsai(CIN AT IT)alian

explanation.surface: Someone spoils a chilli extract at an Italian food counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wreck' reads as a verb, but it is a noun: the most famous shipwreck. Capsaicin is the chemical that makes chillies hot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titanic is the best-known shipwreck of all.

clue.text: Messing up turn, foxtrot’s destroyed (4)

definitions.note: a noun sense: a goof is a messing up, a blunder

indicators.note: one F is knocked out of the phrase

blocks.note: milk that turns goes off: GO OFF
F is foxtrot in the NATO phonetic alphabet; one F is removed

explanation.surface: A dancer botches a turn and the whole foxtrot is ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' belongs to the dance floor in the surface; here it means to go sour, as milk does.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in noun form: a goof is a blunder, the result of messing something up.

clue.text: 1000 senior bears and one other animal (5)

indicators.note: to bear is to carry, so OAP carries K within it

blocks.note: OAP = old-age pensioner, a senior citizen
K = a thousand, as in 10K
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A thousand elderly bears plus one animal of another kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bears' look like animals beside 'other animal', but the word is a verb meaning carries.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is an animal, one other than the bears the surface lists.

clue.text: Tenderfoot left creep during brief amour (10)

indicators.note: the first two pieces happen within the fling

blocks.note: L = left
to edge is to creep forward slowly
a fling is a short affair; L and EDGE go inside after F

explanation.surface: An inexperienced lover abandoned a creepy partner partway through a short romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creep' reads as a nasty person in this romantic surface, but it is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a tenderfoot is a raw novice, and so is a fledgeling, first meaning a young bird just learning to fly.

clue.text: Initially disorganised as butler, I failed to cut pork pie before second course (7,7)

indicators.note: what comes initially in a word is its first letter, so take D from disorganised
the letters have gone wrong, so rearrange them
the jumbled letters cut into the lie
coming before means placed in front, so the lie with its filling precedes S

blocks.note: first letter of disorganised
jumbled together with D to give IBERALSTUD
rhyming slang: pork pie = lie; IBERALSTUD goes inside after L
S = second

explanation.surface: A muddled butler admits he couldn't slice the pork pie before the next course of the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pork pie' is Cockney rhyming slang for lie, often cut to 'porkie'. 'Second course' reads as a dish, but the course is one of study.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal studies is a college course in general arts subjects.

clue.text: Clean, like Em is? (5)

blocks.note: what a bird does to its feathers with its beak
Em is the spelt-out letter M, which sits right before the letter N, spelt en

explanation.walkthrough: 'Em' looks like a name, but it is the spelt-out letter M, which is 'pre-en' because it comes right before N in the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: To preen is to clean and tidy yourself, as a bird does its feathers.

clue.text: Bird’s not drinking in Waikiki, shortly flying East (9)

indicators.note: cut the last letter off Waikiki
the letters fly about, so rearrange them

blocks.note: TT = teetotal
shortened by its last letter
E = East

explanation.surface: A teetotal traveller in Hawaii is soon flying home eastwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Waikiki is the famous beach in Honolulu, Hawaii.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the kittiwake is a small sea gull of northern coasts, one bird among many.

clue.text: Arranging area for party, butcher’s in Hamburg’s terminal embraces joyful circulating (14)

indicators.note: the first three pieces wrap round the fourth
MERRY's letters go round: the M moves from front to back

blocks.note: a butcher's (hook) is Cockney rhyming slang for a look, and so is a gander
used as it is
last letter of Hamburg
MERRY circulates to ERRYM, which goes inside GANDER after its G

explanation.surface: A German butcher's shop gets rearranged for a festive party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher's' looks like a shop but is rhyming slang: 'have a butcher's' means have a look. Gerrymandering is redrawing an electoral district to favour a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerrymandering is arranging an electoral area's boundaries for a party's advantage.

clue.text: Support for those expecting unholy tribes to start to celebrate saint (10)

indicators.note: the letters are wicked and disordered, so rearrange them
take the first letter of celebrate

blocks.note: anagram fodder with C
first letter of celebrate
S = saint

explanation.surface: Heathen tribes about to begin honouring a saint, set against believers waiting for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Those expecting' reads as people waiting, but it means pregnant women.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstetrics is the branch of medicine that cares for pregnant women.

clue.text: Honours for teacher checking cheat’s kept nose clean (7)

indicators.note: BED holds HAVE in check, inside it

blocks.note: a BEd, Bachelor of Education, is a teaching degree
to have someone is to cheat them, as in 'I've been had'

explanation.surface: A teacher's degree awards come from catching a cheat, who has kept out of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Honours' reads as praise, but it is a degree. To keep your nose clean is to stay out of trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to keep your nose clean is to stay out of trouble, which is to have behaved well.

clue.text: What’s possessed rabbit to change direction? (7)

indicators.note: swap one direction letter for another: R (right) becomes L (left)

blocks.note: to rabbit (on) is to chatter; its R becomes L

explanation.surface: A question about what made a rabbit suddenly turn round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' is British slang for talking on and on. 'Possessed' reads as haunted, but it means owned.
explanation.definitionFit: A chattel is a personal possession, something possessed.

clue.text: Earth under rear of fattest cow contracted accordingly (9)

indicators.note: in a down answer, E goes below the rest
the rear of a word is its back end, so take the last letter of fattest
shortened by its last letter

blocks.note: last letter of fattest
a Hereford is a beef breed, cut to HEREFOR
E = Earth

explanation.surface: Soil lies beneath the back of the plumpest cow, which has shrunk as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: HEREFORD loses its D; the Hereford is a red-and-white beef cattle breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Therefore and accordingly both mean as a result.

clue.text: Chinese stuff for poser there (7)

blocks.note: the Tang was a Chinese dynasty
to ram is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: Some Chinese material meant for a model to pose in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poser' reads as someone posing, but it means a puzzle, and 'there' points back to China: a tangram is the Chinese puzzle of seven shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by origin: 'there' refers to the China of 'Chinese', so this is a poser from China, the seven-piece shape puzzle.

clue.text: Hue and cry of Trump supporters guards shut up, not quietly (7)

remove P, piano, quietly in music

blocks.note: Make America Great Again

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hue and cry' reads as a stock phrase for an uproar, but 'Hue' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: magenta is one particular hue, a vivid purplish red.

clue.text: Water source in Germany is screened by research facility (7)

explanation.definitionFit: A cistern stores water and supplies it to a building.

clue.text: Give up immediately after opening three letters in a row (7)

clue.text: Groom never quite nigh for Elizabeth (3,6,5)

clue.text: Fish caught and studied (4)

clue.text: Assume you shouldn’t have asked new nurses about blood group (4,2,4)

indicators.note: the letters are made new, so rearrange them
the jumbled letters nurse, holding RE and A

blocks.note: 'Oh, you shouldn't have!' is what you say for thanks: TA
rearranged, holding RE and A before its D
re = about
A is a blood group

explanation.surface: A patient who asked new nurses about their blood group is told they should not have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You shouldn't have' is what you say on receiving a gift, which makes it a roundabout TA, British slang for thanks.
